subject: Connection fallback plan and customer checklist for US/EU/APAC interruption
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Connection fallback plan and customer checklist for US/EU/APAC interruption

Hi Liam / Acme ops team,

Quick note from our side — we're seeing an upstream networking interruption affecting a subset of regional edge POPs serving US, EU and APAC traffic. Engineering has confirmed the routing fabric at the provider is experiencing packet drops and route flaps for specific availability zones; this is causing elevated request errors and tail latency spikes for a fraction of connections to the hosted endpoint.

What we can do immediately (customer actions that reduce risk while we stabilize):
- Lower client DNS TTL to 60s for your Redwood endpoint (if your infra supports it) so you can pick up alternate IPs faster.
- Enable the SDK endpoint override in your config to direct traffic to the regional fallback endpoint: https://eu-1.fallback.redwood.ai (example).
- If you use our managed edge proxy, flip the region preference in the dashboard to "nearest-available" instead of strict-region routing.
- For long-running streams, switch to the dedicated connection token (we'll issue a short-lived token) which prefers persistent connections to stable hosts.

We've attached a short checklist and a step-by-step reroute PDF with exact commands, DNS records, and SDK snippets. If you'd like, we can schedule a 15-min screen-share now to walk through DNS and the SDK override.

Current status/next steps from Redwood: Monica and Karthik are triaging routing tables and working with the cloud partner support to confirm which AZs are impacted; we will push a forced reroute at the transit layer if partner support agrees. I will follow up with an ETA for the forced transit change within 30 minutes.

Apologies for the disruption — our priority is to keep your production traffic online. Please confirm which fallback you'd like to enable (DNS TTL change + SDK override is the fastest).

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-reroute-step-by-step-v1.pdf (guides commands), acme-fallback-checklist.xlsx (customer checklist)

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acmecorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connection fallback plan and customer checklist for US/EU/APAC interruption

Thanks Rishi — we see the same symptoms from our side (sporadic 5xxs and some connections timing out). We'll take the following now:
- Set DNS TTL to 60s for the next 90 minutes and monitor.
- Apply SDK endpoint override to https://fallback-1.redwood.ai for the web tier (staging first, then prod).

Can you send the SDK snippet for Node and Python? Also, please confirm whether the forced transit reroute will cause any session resets for active websockets (we have a handful of long-lived chat connections).

If switching to override will cause disconnections, we prefer to do a staggered cutover (staging -> canary -> prod) with a 5-min window between stages.

— Liam
Ops Lead, AcmeCorp

On Mon, Jun 18, 2028 at 09:12 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connection fallback plan and customer checklist for US/EU/APAC interruption

Rishi — update from infra: partner support confirmed two transit routers in EU-west2 and one router in APAC-south1 are exhibiting BGP instability; provider is rolling config fix but timeline is uncertain (est. 45-90m).

What we propose on Redwood side:
- Force route preference change at the edge for affected customers (non-disruptive for short HTTP requests; websocket connections will terminate and reconnect).
- Issue short-lived persistent tokens for WebSocket workflows to favor the dedicated connection path (reduces reconnect retries).
- Provide Node/Python SDK snippet we tested for override; see drive link in related_links.

I'll prepare the canary plan: do staging -> 2% prod -> 10% -> 100% with 5m observation windows. Lauren, can you approve the customer communication template for a quick follow-up?

Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Liam — quick status and next actions: 
1) We executed a controlled canary at 11:20 PT (staging -> 2% prod). No regressions observed; websocket reconnect rate was within expected limits.
2) We've issued the Node and Python SDK override snippets and a short-lived WS token to your security team via separate secure message.
3) Recommended plan for Acme right now:
   - Continue with DNS TTL 60s for 90 minutes.
   - Apply SDK override in prod at 14:00 PT in a staged manner (2% -> 10% -> 100%), 5m observation windows.
   - If you prefer Redwood to perform the transit-level reroute, we can do that at 15:00 PT; note that will cause active websocket connections to drop and reconnect.

I'll leave the attachments and the drive link for the detailed commands. We will keep the ticket INC-9241 updated and notify you immediately if provider confirms full convergence. 

If anything changes before 15:00 PT, I'll ping you and coordinate a tighter window. Thanks for the quick coordination.

Best,
Rishi

Redwood Inference
